description: AI productivity agent that connects work apps, writes code to complete tasks, and turns recurring workflows into reusable and shareable Playbooks.

evidence.finding: Lutra's terms say users control how much information from connected third-party accounts is accessible by adjusting privacy settings on those accounts.
Lutra's terms say users can revoke the private-content license by deleting the relevant content or terminating their account, subject to retention and legal requirements.
Lutra states that users have full visibility into actions and generated code, and its help center explains that Lutra writes code to execute tasks reproducibly.
Lutra's terms state that users are given an opportunity to review and confirm generated content before execution.
Lutra offers a free plan and publishes usage-based credit pricing so individuals can try the automation service before upgrading.
Lutra's terms state that private user submissions remain owned by the user and are private by default.
Lutra's terms allow private submissions from non-paid users to be used for training or improving its services, which weakens the data-rights signal for free users.
Lutra supports custom integrations through MCP, REST, OpenAPI, databases, and many third-party productivity tools, providing multiple integration paths.
Lutra describes a simple pricing model with flat subscription access and credit-based usage, with extra discounted credits available on higher plans.
Lutra lets users save and share Playbooks with teammates, and enterprise users can share playbooks organization-wide to standardize work.
Lutra's terms preserve human review before generated content executes, reducing the risk that consequential automation proceeds without user confirmation.
Lutra offers a free plan and natural-language automation that can generate integrations and workflows without requiring users to write the code themselves.

limitations: This preliminary audit uses public Lutra AI primary-source documentation and has not been reviewed by Lutra AI.
Published product documentation is evidence of documented controls and policies, not proof of real-world outcomes for every deployment.
Humanity Score is a product-impact rating, not a regulatory, legal, safety, compliance, or government certification.
correction_policy: Source-backed factual corrections are welcome. Corrections change the audit only when the underlying evidence changes; payment cannot buy a higher score.
